name: Earth Planetary Sciences (Min)

rules.name: Earth and Planetary Sciences Foundation (18 units)
rules.desc: Students must complete 5 courses that introduce the properties of planetary materials, the processes that change the Earth and other planets, and the timescales over which those processes act. These courses provide a broad foundational knowledge that can lead to specialization in many different geological and environmental sciences disciplines.

rules.name: Breadth in Discipline (9 units)
rules.desc:
Students select from a range of elective 100-level geoscience courses, offering exposure to diverse fields. These courses include classroom lectures, often supplemented with field and laboratory components. Students must take a minimum of 9 additional units drawn primarily from the Breadth in the Discipline list in the EPS major; a majority of units must be from classes within the EPS department.

• Courses such as EPS 20, EPS 30N, EPS 38N, EPS 42, EPS 40N, and EPS 45 can contribute towards fulfilling the Breadth in Discipline requirement.

• Classic geology courses are highly recommended by faculty and students (EPS 101, 102, 104, 111)

gpa: Stanford undergraduates must maintain a minimum 2.0 cumulative GPA to remain in good academic standing and graduate. While the university calculates GPA using a traditional 4.0 scale, competitive admissions averages hover near a 3.94, and individual class rankings are not calculated
grading: Students are responsible for checking their final grades at the end of each quarter. If incomplete grades (I), Grade Not Reported (GNR), or No Credit (NC) appear on the end-of-quarter grade report, students should immediately check with their instructor. The Assistant Director of Student Services can assist students and instructors in clearing missing and incomplete grades by forwarding the appropriate instructions and/or university forms.
transferPolicy: No external transfer or test credit is accepted for this minor
reviewNotes: The minor is the five foundation courses (EPS 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6) and 9 units of breadth courses with a majority, at least 5 units, in EPS, for 27 units. Courses from outside the breadth list are moved in by hand, your advisor checks the 2.0 GPA, and transfer or test credit does not count. The Bulletin calls the foundation 18 units, but its five courses carry 17 in the catalog, so a minor with exactly 9 breadth units comes to 26 and needs one more unit toward the 27.
